title: Raw Dart StateError text leaks into a user-facing error toast
what_happened: Pressing 'Test' on 'Test push notification' with no remote access running produced the toast: 'Failed to send test notification: Bad state: No push transport is listening. Start remote access before testing.' The 'Bad state:' prefix is StateError.toString() bleeding through into shipped copy.
expected: 'Failed to send test notification: no push transport is listening. Start remote access before testing.' The message content is good and actionable -- only the exception prefix is wrong.
repro: Settings > NOTIFICATIONS & REMOTE > Notifications > scroll to 'Push to Mobile' > 'Test push notification' > Test.
where: notification test-push handler in packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/widgets/notification_settings.dart (catch block interpolating the raw error)
proposed_fix: Catch StateError specifically and surface e.message, or strip the 'Bad state: ' prefix before interpolating.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced exactly. Settings > Notifications > Push to Mobile > 'Test push notification' > Test produced the red toast 'Failed to send test notification: Bad state: No push transport is listening. Start remote access before testing.' (shot /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sov-20-testpush.png). Source path matches: push_notification_service.dart:182-186 throws StateError('No push transport is listening. Start remote access before testing.') and notification_settings.dart:197 interpolates the object with `'Failed to send test notification: $e'`, so StateError.toString()'s 'Bad state: ' prefix reaches shipped copy. P3 is right — cosmetic, the message is otherwise accurate and actionable.

title: Dead/duplicated settings keys persist and are exported while no UI reflects them
what_happened: Two cases found by diffing the UI against the scratch DB. (1) app_settings.auto_save_sequences = 'true' (its shipped default) coexists with autosave.sequence_enabled = 'false', which is what the Files & Storage toggle showed and what AutoSaveService actually obeys. No UI surfaces auto_save_sequences, but it is written into settings snapshots/exports and served through the app-settings model, so a remote/web surface reading it reports sequence auto-save ON while the desktop has it OFF. (2) app_settings.plate_solver = 'ASTAP' coexists with the Plate Solving page's 'Active solver' radio (Auto-fallback), which is backed by Rust platesolver.json via plateSolverPreferenceProvider. Confusingly the Solve Parameters on that same page DO write sqlite -- I typed 45 into Timeout and plate_solve_timeout went 60 -> 45 -- so one page writes two different stores.
expected: One store per logical setting. Anything that rides export/backup/API should be the value the app actually obeys.
repro: Fresh profile. Settings > Files & Storage > AUTO-SAVE & BACKUPS: 'Enable sequence auto-save' reads OFF. Then `sqlite3 <profile>/data/skotiq.db "select key,value from app_settings where key like '%auto_save%' or key like 'autosave%'"`. Same for plate_solver vs the Active solver radio.
evidence: sqlite output: auto_save_sequences|true alongside autosave.sequence_enabled|false; plate_solver|ASTAP alongside a UI showing Auto-fallback. /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-59-files.png (toggle OFF), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-67-verify.png (Auto-fallback selected). Export path is source-only.
proposed_fix: Either delete auto_save_sequences / plate_solver from default_settings.dart and the snapshot mapping, or make the AppSettings getters read through to autosave.sequence_enabled and the Rust platesolver preference so the exported value is the obeyed value.
verdict_reasoning: Case (1) confirmed. My fresh profile's DB holds auto_save_sequences|true while the Files & Storage 'Enable sequence auto-save' toggle reads OFF (shot sov-02-files.png; AutoSaveConfig.sequenceEnabled defaults false and autosave.sequence_enabled is unset). setAutoSaveSequences exists (settings_sections/general.dart:27-30) but grep across packages/skotiq_app/lib finds ZERO callers, and nothing reads state.autoSaveSequences for behaviour — yet app_settings_stored_snapshot_mapping.dart:515 rewrites it on every settings save and BackupService._exportSettings (backup_service.dart:711-715) dumps the whole app_settings table into every .nsbackup. So it is a dead key that is persisted and exported. Case (2) confirmed as a two-store split: plate_solver|ASTAP lives in sqlite with no UI, while the page's Active-solver control is backed by plateSolverPreferenceProvider -> Rust platesolver.json (plate_solver_provider.dart:18-25), and the Solve Parameters on that same page DO write sqlite (plate_solve_parameters_section.dart:87-88 setPlateSolveTimeout; my DB shows plate_solve_timeout|60). TWO CORRECTIONS to the finding's reasoning. (a) The stated consequence for case 1 is unsupported: autoSaveSequences appears nowhere in models/settings/app_settings.dart or app_settings_remote_mapping.dart, so no remote/web surface serves it — the exposure is backup/export files only. (b) 'plate_solver' is NOT dead: default_science_backend/helpers.dart:663-666 _resolveSolverId() returns settings.plateSolver, and app_settings_remote_mapping.dart:651-652 lets a remote client set it — which makes the split arguably a real correctness bug (science labels solves 'ASTAP' while the actual engine preference is auto-fallback), not just tidy-up. Keeping P3.
